title.zh: 卷七十六 志第二十九 律曆九
title.raw: 卷七十六 志第二十九 律曆九 Volume 76 Treatises 29: Measures and Calendar 9

sentences.zh: 皇祐渾儀

translations.literal: Huangyou Armillary Sphere
translations.idiomatic: The Huangyou Armillary Sphere

sentences.zh: 堯敕羲和制橫簫以考察星度，其機衡用玉，欲其燥濕不變，運動有常，堅久而不能廢也。

translations.literal: Yao commanded Xihe to make transverse sight-tubes to examine the degrees of the stars; its mechanisms and pivots used jade, wishing that dryness and moisture would not alter it, that motion would have constancy, and that it would be firm and long-lasting and could not be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Yao charged Xihe with fashioning transverse sight-tubes to measure the stars, and had the mechanisms and pivots made of jade so they would not warp with damp or dryness, would move evenly, and would endure firm and unchanging for long use.

sentences.zh: 至於後世，鑄銅為圓儀，以法天體。

translations.literal: As for later generations, they cast copper into a spherical instrument to model the heavenly body.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, bronze was cast into a spherical instrument to represent the celestial sphere.

sentences.zh: 自洛下閎造《太初曆》，用渾儀，及東漢孝和帝時，太史惟有赤道儀，歲時測候，頗有進退。

translations.literal: From when Luoxia Hong made the Taichu Calendar and used the armillary sphere, until the time of Emperor Xiaohe of the Eastern Han, the Grand Astrologer had only an equatorial instrument; seasonal measurements and observations had considerable advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: From Luoxia Hong's compilation of the Taichu Calendar with the armillary sphere down to the Eastern Han Emperor He, the Grand Astrologer's office possessed only an equatorial instrument, and its seasonal observations drifted noticeably.

sentences.zh: 帝以問典星待詔姚崇等，皆曰：「星圖有規法，日月實從黃道，今無其器，是以失之。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired of the Palace Star Awaited-Edict Yao Chong and others; all said: "The star chart has regulated methods; sun and moon in fact follow the Yellow Path; now we lack its instrument, and for this reason we have missed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the awaited-edict astrologers Yao Chong and others, and they all replied: "The star chart follows fixed rules, and the sun and moon truly travel the ecliptic; because we lack the proper instrument today, our readings go astray."

sentences.zh: 」至永元十五年，賈逵始設黃道儀。

translations.literal: " By the fifteenth year of Yongyuan, Jia Kui first set up an ecliptic instrument.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yongyuan (103 CE), Jia Kui first installed an ecliptic instrument.

sentences.zh: 桓帝延熹七年，張衡更制之，以四分為度。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanxi under Emperor Huan, Zhang Heng remade it, taking one quarter as a degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yanxi (164 CE) under Emperor Huan, Zhang Heng redesigned it, using quarter-degrees as the unit.

sentences.zh: 其後，陸績、王蕃、孔挺、斛蘭、梁令瓚、李淳風並嘗製作。

translations.literal: Afterward, Lu Ji, Wang Fan, Kong Ting, Hu Lan, Liang Lingzan, and Li Chunfeng all at times made versions.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Lu Ji, Wang Fan, Kong Ting, Hu Lan, Liang Lingzan, and Li Chunfeng each produced instruments of their own.

sentences.zh: 五代亂亡，遺法蕩然矣。

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties fell in disorder and ruin, and the transmitted methods were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: The turmoil and collapse of the Five Dynasties swept away the transmitted methods entirely.

sentences.zh: 真宗祥符初，韓顯符作渾儀，但遊儀雙環夾望筒旋轉，而黃、赤道相固不動。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiangfu under Emperor Zhenzong, Han Xianfu made an armillary sphere, but only the pivoting instrument's double rings clamping the sight-tube rotated, while the Yellow Path and equator rings were fixed and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiangfu era under Emperor Zhenzong, Han Xianfu built an armillary sphere in which only the pivoting rings gripping the sight-tube could turn, while the ecliptic and equatorial rings remained fixed.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，又命日官舒易簡、于淵、周琮等參用淳風、令瓚之制，改鑄黃道渾儀，又為漏刻、圭表，詔翰林學士錢明逸詳其法，內侍麥允言總其工。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangyou, the court again ordered the solar officials Shu Yijian, Yu Yuan, Zhou Cong, and others to consult the designs of Chunfeng and Lingzan, recast an ecliptic armillary sphere, and also make clepsydra graduations and a gnomon table; an edict directed Hanlin Academician Qian Mingyi to elaborate the methods, and Inner Attendant Mai Yunyan to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangyou era, the court again ordered the solar officials Shu Yijian, Yu Yuan, and Zhou Cong to draw on the designs of Li Chunfeng and Liang Lingzan, recast an ecliptic armillary sphere, and also build clepsydra graduations and a gnomon table; Hanlin Academician Qian Mingyi was directed to work out the methods, and Inner Attendant Mai Yunyan to supervise construction.

sentences.zh: 既成，置渾儀于翰林天文院之候台，漏刻於文德殿之鐘鼓樓，圭表于司天監。

translations.literal: When completed, the armillary sphere was placed on the observation terrace of the Hanlin Astronomical Bureau, the clepsydra graduations in the bell-and-drum tower of Wende Hall, and the gnomon table at the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: When they were finished, the armillary sphere was installed on the observation terrace of the Hanlin Astronomical Bureau, the clepsydra in the bell-and-drum tower of Wende Hall, and the gnomon table at the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 帝為制《渾儀總要》十卷，論前代得失，已而留中不出。

translations.literal: The emperor composed Essentials of the Armillary Sphere in ten scrolls, discussing the gains and losses of former ages, but afterward kept it within the palace and did not release it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drafted Essentials of the Armillary Sphere in ten scrolls, reviewing what earlier ages had done well or poorly, but afterward kept the work in the palace archives and never published it.

sentences.zh: 今具黃道遊儀之法，著於此焉。

translations.literal: Now the methods of the ecliptic pivoting instrument are set forth in full and recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The methods of the ecliptic pivoting instrument are set forth in full below.

sentences.zh: 第一重，名六合儀。

translations.literal: The first layer, named the Six Harmonies Instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The first layer is called the Six Harmonies Instrument.

sentences.zh: 陽經雙環：週邊二丈三尺二寸八分，直徑七尺七寸六分，闊六寸，厚六分。

translations.literal: Yang meridian double ring: circumference 2 zhang 3 chi 2 cun 8 fen, diameter 7 chi 7 cun 6 fen, width 6 cun, thickness 6 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang meridian double ring: circumference 2 zhang 3 chi 2 cun 8 fen, diameter 7 chi 7 cun 6 fen, width 6 cun, thickness 6 fen.

sentences.zh: 南北並立，兩面各列周天三百六十五度少強，北極出地三十五度少強。

translations.literal: Standing north and south together, on both faces are marked the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees, with the north pole 35 and a fraction degrees above the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Set upright north and south, each face marked with the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees, and the north celestial pole 35 and a fraction degrees above the horizon.

sentences.zh: 陰緯單環：週邊、徑、闊與陽經雙環等，外厚二寸五分，內厚一寸九分。

translations.literal: Yin latitude single ring: circumference, diameter, and width equal to the yang meridian double ring; outer thickness 2 cun 5 fen, inner thickness 1 cun 9 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin latitude single ring: circumference, diameter, and width match the yang meridian double ring; outer thickness 2 cun 5 fen, inner thickness 1 cun 9 fen.

sentences.zh: 上列十幹、十二支、八封方位，以正地形。

translations.literal: On it are marked the ten stems, twelve branches, and eight trigram directions to align the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: It bears the ten heavenly stems, twelve earthly branches, and eight trigram directions to orient the instrument to the ground.

sentences.zh: 上有池沿環流轉，以定平准。

translations.literal: Above is a channel rim with water circulating around it to set level and true.
translations.idiomatic: A channel rim above circulates water to establish true level.

sentences.zh: 天常單環：週邊二丈四寸六分，直徑六尺八寸二分，闊、厚一寸二分。

translations.literal: Heaven's constant single ring: circumference 2 zhang 4 cun 6 fen, diameter 6 chi 8 cun 2 fen, width and thickness 1 cun 2 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's constant single ring: circumference 2 zhang 4 cun 6 fen, diameter 6 chi 8 cun 2 fen, width and thickness each 1 cun 2 fen.

sentences.zh: 上列十幹、十二支、四維時刻之數，以測辰刻，與陽經、陰緯環相固，如卵之殼幕然。

translations.literal: On it are marked the ten stems, twelve branches, and the numbers of the four corner hours to measure the double-hours and clepsydra marks; it is fixed to the yang meridian and yin latitude rings like an eggshell membrane.
translations.idiomatic: It bears the ten stems, twelve branches, and corner-hour divisions for measuring double-hours and clepsydra marks, fixed to the yang meridian and yin latitude rings like a shell around an egg.

sentences.zh: 第二重，名三辰儀。

translations.literal: The second layer, named the Three Luminaries Instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The second layer is called the Three Luminaries Instrument.

sentences.zh: 璿璣雙環：週邊一丈九尺五寸六分，直徑六尺五寸二分，闊一寸四分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: Xuanji double ring: circumference 1 zhang 9 chi 5 cun 6 fen, diameter 6 chi 5 cun 2 fen, width 1 cun 4 fen, thickness 1 cun.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanji double ring: circumference 1 zhang 9 chi 5 cun 6 fen, diameter 6 chi 5 cun 2 fen, width 1 cun 4 fen, thickness 1 cun.

sentences.zh: 兩面各均周天三百六十五度少強，作二樞對兩極。

translations.literal: On both faces the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees is evenly divided, making two pivots facing the two poles.
translations.idiomatic: Each face is evenly graduated for the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees, with two pivots set opposite the celestial poles.

sentences.zh: 赤道單環：週邊一丈九尺六寸八分，直徑六尺五寸六分，闊一寸一分，厚六分。

translations.literal: Equator single ring: circumference 1 zhang 9 chi 6 cun 8 fen, diameter 6 chi 5 cun 6 fen, width 1 cun 1 fen, thickness 6 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Equatorial single ring: circumference 1 zhang 9 chi 6 cun 8 fen, diameter 6 chi 5 cun 6 fen, width 1 cun 1 fen, thickness 6 fen.

sentences.zh: 上列二十八宿距度、周天三百六十五度少強，附於璿璣之上。

translations.literal: On it are marked the interval degrees of the twenty-eight lodges and the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees, attached upon the Xuanji ring.
translations.idiomatic: It bears the interval degrees of the twenty-eight lunar lodges and the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees, mounted on the Xuanji ring.

sentences.zh: 黃道單環：週邊一丈九尺二分，直徑六尺三寸四分，闊一寸二分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: Yellow Path single ring: circumference 1 zhang 9 chi 2 fen, diameter 6 chi 3 cun 4 fen, width 1 cun 2 fen, thickness 1 cun.
translations.idiomatic: Ecliptic single ring: circumference 1 zhang 9 chi 2 fen, diameter 6 chi 3 cun 4 fen, width 1 cun 2 fen, thickness 1 cun.

sentences.zh: 上列周天三百六十五度少強，均分二十四氣、七十二候、六十四卦、三百六十策。

translations.literal: On it are marked the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees, evenly divided into the twenty-four qi, seventy-two hou, sixty-four hexagrams, and three hundred sixty counting rods.
translations.idiomatic: It bears the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees, evenly divided into the twenty-four solar terms, seventy-two pentads, sixty-four hexagrams, and three hundred sixty yarrow stalks.

sentences.zh: 出入赤道二十四度，與赤道相交，每歲退差一分有餘。

translations.literal: It enters and exits the equator by twenty-four degrees, intersecting the equator; each year it retreats in discrepancy by more than one degree.
translations.idiomatic: It inclines twenty-four degrees to the equator and crosses it, precessing backward by more than one degree each year.

sentences.zh: 白道單環：週邊一丈八尺六寸三分，直徑六尺二寸一分，闊一寸一分，厚五分。

translations.literal: White Path single ring: circumference 1 zhang 8 chi 6 cun 3 fen, diameter 6 chi 2 cun 1 fen, width 1 cun 1 fen, thickness 5 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar path single ring: circumference 1 zhang 8 chi 6 cun 3 fen, diameter 6 chi 2 cun 1 fen, width 1 cun 1 fen, thickness 5 fen.

sentences.zh: 上列交度，置於黃道環中，入黃道六度，每一交終，退行黃道一度半弱，皆旋轉於六合之內。

translations.literal: On it are marked the crossing degrees, set within the Yellow Path ring, entering the Yellow Path by six degrees; at each crossing's end it retreats along the Yellow Path by one and a fraction degrees; all rotate within the Six Harmonies.
translations.idiomatic: It bears the nodal degrees, set inside the ecliptic ring, inclined six degrees to the ecliptic; at the end of each nodal cycle it regresses along the ecliptic by one and a fraction degrees; all these rings turn within the Six Harmonies layer.

sentences.zh: 第三重，名四遊儀。

translations.literal: The third layer, named the Four Pivots Instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The third layer is called the Four Pivots Instrument.

sentences.zh: 璿樞雙環：週邊一丈八尺二寸一分，直徑六尺七分，闊二寸，厚七分。

translations.literal: Xuanshu double ring: circumference 1 zhang 8 chi 2 cun 1 fen, diameter 6 chi 7 fen, width 2 cun, thickness 7 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshu double ring: circumference 1 zhang 8 chi 2 cun 1 fen, diameter 6 chi 7 fen, width 2 cun, thickness 7 fen.

sentences.zh: 兩面各列周天三百六十五度少強，挾直距以對樞軸，東西運轉於三辰儀內，以格星度。

translations.literal: On both faces are marked the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees; clamping the straight arm to face the pivot axis, it turns east and west within the Three Luminaries Instrument to measure star degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Each face is graduated for the full circuit of 365 and a fraction degrees; gripping the sight arm against the pivot axis, it rotates east and west within the Three Luminaries layer to take star positions.

sentences.zh: 橫簫望筒：長五尺七寸，外方內圓，中通望孔，直徑六分，周於日輪，在璿樞直距之中，使南北遊仰，以窺辰宿，無所不至。

translations.literal: Transverse flute sight-tube: length 5 chi 7 cun, square outside and round inside, with a sight hole through the center, diameter 6 fen, encircling the solar disc; set in the Xuanshu straight arm, it allows north-south pivoting and elevation to observe stars and lodges, reaching everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Transverse sight-tube: five chi seven cun long, square outside and round inside, with a central sight hole six fen across, aligned with the solar disc; mounted in the Xuanshu sight arm, it pivots north-south and tilts up and down to sight any star or lodge.

sentences.zh: 十字水準槽：長九尺四寸八分，首闊一尺二寸七分，身闊九寸二分、高七尺。

translations.literal: Cross-shaped leveling trough: length 9 chi 4 cun 8 fen, head width 1 chi 2 cun 7 fen, body width 9 cun 2 fen, height 7 chi.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-shaped leveling trough: length 9 chi 4 cun 8 fen, head width 1 chi 2 cun 7 fen, body width 9 cun 2 fen, height 7 chi.

sentences.zh: 水槽一寸，深八分，四柱各長六尺七寸八分，植于水槽之末，以輔天體，皆以銅為之。

translations.literal: The trough channel is 1 cun wide and 8 fen deep; the four pillars are each 6 chi 7 cun 8 fen long, planted at the ends of the trough to support the heavenly body; all are made of bronze.
translations.idiomatic: The trough is one cun wide and eight fen deep; four pillars, each six chi seven cun eight fen long, stand at the ends of the trough to bear the celestial assembly; all are cast in bronze.

sentences.zh: 乃格七曜遠近盈縮，以知晝夜長短之效。

translations.literal: Thus it measures the seven luminaries' distance, nearness, fullness, and shrinkage to know the effect of day and night length.
translations.idiomatic: In this way it gauges the seven luminaries' distances and phases of waxing and waning, revealing how day and night lengthen and shorten.

sentences.zh: 其所測二十八舍距度，著於後；

translations.literal: The interval degrees of the twenty-eight lodges that it measures are recorded afterward;
translations.idiomatic: The interval degrees of the twenty-eight lodges measured with it are recorded below;

sentences.zh: 其周天星入宿去極所主吉凶，則具在《天文志》。

translations.literal: As for the stars of the full circuit entering lodges, distance from the pole, and the auspice or bale they govern, these are fully set out in the Treatise on Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The stars' lodge entries, polar distances, and the fortunes they govern are set out fully in the Treatise on Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 角十二度，亢九度，氐十六度，房五度，心四度，尾十九度，箕十度，鬥二十五度，牛七度，女十一度，虛十度，危十六度，室十七度，壁九度，奎十六度，婁十二度，胃十五度，昴十一度，畢十八度，觜一度，參十度，井三十四度，鬼二度，柳十四度，星七度，張十八度，翼十八度，軫十七度。

translations.literal: Horn twelve degrees, Neck nine degrees, Root sixteen degrees, Chamber five degrees, Heart four degrees, Tail nineteen degrees, Winnowing-basket ten degrees, Dipper twenty-five degrees, Ox seven degrees, Maid eleven degrees, Void ten degrees, Rooftop sixteen degrees, Encampment seventeen degrees, Wall nine degrees, Legs sixteen degrees, Bond twelve degrees, Stomach fifteen degrees, Hairy Head eleven degrees, Net eighteen degrees, Turtle Beak one degree, Three Stars ten degrees, Well thirty-four degrees, Ghost two degrees, Willow fourteen degrees, Star seven degrees, Extended Net eighteen degrees, Wings eighteen degrees, Chariot Axle seventeen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Horn: 12°; Neck: 9°; Root: 16°; Chamber: 5°; Heart: 4°; Tail: 19°; Winnowing-basket: 10°; Dipper: 25°; Ox: 7°; Maid: 11°; Void: 10°; Rooftop: 16°; Encampment: 17°; Wall: 9°; Legs: 16°; Bond: 12°; Stomach: 15°; Hairy Head: 11°; Net: 18°; Turtle Beak: 1°; Three Stars: 10°; Well: 34°; Ghost: 2°; Willow: 14°; Star: 7°; Extended Net: 18°; Wings: 18°; Chariot Axle: 17°.

sentences.zh: 皇祐漏刻

translations.literal: Huangyou Clepsydra Graduations
translations.idiomatic: The Huangyou Clepsydra Graduations

sentences.zh: 自黃帝觀漏水，制器取則，三代因以命官，則挈壺氏其職也。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor's observation of dripping water and making instruments to take standards, the Three Dynasties accordingly appointed officials, and the Qiehu clan held that office.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor's observation of dripping water and devising instruments to set standards, the Three Dynasties appointed officials to the task—the Qiehu clan held that charge.

sentences.zh: 後之作者，或下漏，或浮漏，或輪漏，或權衡，製作不一。

translations.literal: Later makers used either descending clepsydra, floating clepsydra, wheel clepsydra, or balance-and-weight types; the constructions were not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Later makers devised descending clepsydras, floating clepsydras, wheel clepsydras, or balance-and-weight clocks—the designs varied widely.

sentences.zh: 宋舊有刻漏及以水為權衡，置文德殿之東廡。

translations.literal: The Song formerly had graduated clepsydra and water-as-balance types, placed in the east wing of Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court already possessed graduated clepsydras and water-balance clocks, kept in the east wing of Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，再加考定，而水有遲疾，用有司之請，增平水壺一、渴烏二、晝夜箭二十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou it was examined and fixed again, but the water had slow and fast flow; following the responsible office's request, one level-water jar, two thirsty-bird siphons, and twenty-one day-and-night arrows were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingyou (1036) it was recalibrated, yet the water still ran unevenly; at the responsible office's request, one leveling jar, two siphon birds, and twenty-one day-and-night arrows were added.

sentences.zh: 然常以四時日出傳卯正一刻，又每時正已傳一刻，至八刻已傳次時，即二時初末相侵殆半。

translations.literal: Yet it regularly took the four seasons' sunrise to transmit the first mark of mao proper, and at each double-hour's proper mark one mark was already transmitted; by the eighth mark the next double-hour was already transmitted—thus the beginning and end of two double-hours encroached on each other by nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it routinely took sunrise in each season to signal the first mark of mao proper, and by each double-hour's proper mark one mark had already been struck; by the eighth mark the next double-hour was sounding—so the start and end of successive double-hours overlapped by nearly half.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，詔舒易簡、于淵、周琮更造，其法用平水重壺均調水勢，使無遲疾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangyou, an edict ordered Shu Yijian, Yu Yuan, and Zhou Cong to remake it; the method used a level-water weighted jar to equalize the water's force so there would be no slow or fast flow.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangyou, an edict directed Shu Yijian, Yu Yuan, and Zhou Cong to rebuild the clock; their method used a leveling weighted jar to steady the flow and eliminate uneven dripping.

sentences.zh: 分百刻於晝夜；

translations.literal: It divided one hundred marks between day and night;
translations.idiomatic: The day and night were divided into one hundred marks;

sentences.zh: 冬至晝漏四十刻，夜漏六十刻；

translations.literal: at winter solstice day clepsydra forty marks, night clepsydra sixty marks;
translations.idiomatic: at winter solstice, forty marks by day and sixty by night;

sentences.zh: 夏至晝漏六十刻，夜漏四十刻；

translations.literal: at summer solstice day clepsydra sixty marks, night clepsydra forty marks;
translations.idiomatic: at summer solstice, sixty marks by day and forty by night;

sentences.zh: 春秋二分晝夜各五十刻。

translations.literal: at spring and autumn equinoxes day and night each fifty marks.
translations.idiomatic: at the spring and autumn equinoxes, day and night each received fifty marks.

sentences.zh: 日未出前二刻半為曉，日沒後二刻半為昏，減夜五刻以益晝漏，謂之昏旦漏刻。

translations.literal: Two and a half marks before the sun's rising was dawn; two and a half marks after the sun's setting was dusk; five marks were subtracted from night to add to day clepsydra—called the dusk-and-dawn clepsydra marks.
translations.idiomatic: Two and a half marks before sunrise counted as dawn, and two and a half after sunset as dusk; five marks were shifted from night to day—this was called the dusk-and-dawn clepsydra adjustment.

sentences.zh: 皆隨氣增損焉。

translations.literal: All increased or decreased according to the qi.
translations.idiomatic: All varied with the solar terms.

sentences.zh: 冬至、夏至之間，晝夜長短凡差二十刻，每差一刻，別為一箭，冬至互起其首，凡有四十一箭。

translations.literal: Between winter and summer solstices, day and night length in all differed by twenty marks; for each mark of difference a separate arrow was made; winter solstice alternately began the sequence—in all forty-one arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Between winter and summer solstice the day-night span differed by twenty marks in all; each mark's difference had its own arrow, the sequence starting alternately from winter solstice—forty-one arrows in total.

sentences.zh: 晝有朝、有禺、有中、有晡、有夕，夜有甲、乙、丙、丁、戊，昏旦有星中，每箭各異其數。

translations.literal: Day had morning, yu, noon, bu, and evening; night had jia, yi, bing, ding, and wu; dusk and dawn had stars at culmination—each arrow had different numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Day was divided into morning, mid-morning, noon, afternoon, and evening; night into the five watches jia through wu; dusk and dawn had culminating stars—each arrow bore its own set of figures.

sentences.zh: 凡黃道升降差二度四十分，則隨曆增減改箭。

translations.literal: Whenever the Yellow Path's rising and falling differed by two degrees forty minutes, the arrows were increased or decreased following the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the ecliptic's elevation changed by two degrees forty minutes, the arrows were adjusted to match the calendar.

sentences.zh: 每時初行一刻至四刻六分之一為時正，終八刻六分之二則交次時。

translations.literal: At each double-hour's beginning, from one mark to four and one-sixth marks was the double-hour's proper mark; ending at eight and two-sixths marks it crossed to the next double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Each double-hour began with one mark and reached its proper mark at four and one-sixth marks; at eight and two-sixths marks it passed into the next double-hour.

sentences.zh: 今列二十四氣、晝夜日出入辰刻、昏曉中星，以備參合。

translations.literal: Now are listed the twenty-four qi, day and night sun rise and set with double-hours and marks, and dusk and dawn culminating stars, for reference and comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Below are tabulated the twenty-four solar terms, day and night lengths with sunrise and sunset marks, and dusk and dawn culminating stars for cross-reference.

sentences.zh: 皇祐圭表

translations.literal: Huangyou Gnomon Table
translations.idiomatic: The Huangyou Gnomon Table

sentences.zh: 觀天地陰陽之體，以正位辨方、定時考閏，莫近乎圭表。

translations.literal: To observe heaven and earth's yin-yang substance, to set position and distinguish directions, fix seasons and examine intercalation—nothing comes closer than the gnomon table.
translations.idiomatic: To read heaven and earth's yin-yang pattern, fix position and direction, and set seasons and intercalation, nothing serves better than the gnomon table.

sentences.zh: 宋何承天始立表候日景，十年間，知冬至比舊用《景初曆》常後天三日。

translations.literal: In Song, He Chengtian first set up a table to observe the sun's shadow; over ten years he learned that winter solstice compared with the old Jingchu Calendar regularly lagged heaven by three days.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, He Chengtian first erected a gnomon to observe solar shadows; within ten years he found that winter solstice by the old Jingchu Calendar regularly lagged the heavens by three days.

sentences.zh: 又唐一行造《大衍曆》，用圭表測知舊曆氣節常後天一日。

translations.literal: Again, in Tang Yixing made the Dayan Calendar; using the gnomon table he measured and knew the old calendar's qi and nodes regularly lagged heaven by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in Tang times Yixing compiled the Dayan Calendar and, measuring with the gnomon table, found the old calendar's solar terms regularly lagged the heavens by one day.

sentences.zh: 今司天監圭表乃石晉時天文參謀趙延乂所建，表既欹傾，圭亦墊陷，其於天度無所取正。

translations.literal: Now the Directorate of Astronomy's gnomon table was built by astronomical adviser Zhao Yanyi of Later Jin; the table was already leaning, the gnomon also sunk and tilted, and for celestial degrees it took no correct standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate's present gnomon table was built by Later Jin astronomical adviser Zhao Yanyi; the table had tilted and the gnomon platform had sunk and shifted, so it could no longer fix celestial degrees accurately.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，詔周琮、于淵、舒易簡改制之，乃考古法，立八尺銅表，厚二寸，博四寸，下連石圭一丈三尺，以盡冬至景長之數，面有雙水溝為平准，於溝雙刻尺寸分數，又刻二十四氣岳台晷景所得尺寸，置於司天監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangyou, an edict ordered Zhou Cong, Yu Yuan, and Shu Yijian to remake it; they examined ancient methods, set up an eight-chi bronze table two cun thick and four cun wide, joined below to a stone gnomon one zhang three chi to exhaust winter solstice shadow length, with double water channels on the face for leveling, on the channels doubly engraved inches, cun, and fen, and also engraved the twenty-four qi's gnomon-shadow dimensions obtained at Yue Terrace, placed at the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangyou, Zhou Cong, Yu Yuan, and Shu Yijian were ordered to rebuild it; studying ancient methods, they erected an eight-chi bronze gnomon two cun thick and four cun wide, joined to a stone platform one zhang three chi long to capture the full winter-solstice shadow, with twin water channels on the face for leveling and graduated inches, cun, and fen on both sides, plus the twenty-four solar terms' shadow lengths measured at Yue Terrace; the instrument was installed at the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 候之三年，知氣節比舊曆後天半日。

translations.literal: Observing for three years, they knew the qi and nodes lagged heaven by half a day compared with the old calendar.
translations.idiomatic: After three years of observation, they found the solar terms lagged the heavens by half a day compared with the old calendar.

sentences.zh: 因而成書三卷，命曰《岳台晷景新書》論前代測候是非、步算之法頗詳。

translations.literal: Thereupon they completed a book in three scrolls, titled New Book of Yue Terrace Gnomon Shadows, discussing former ages' measurement right and wrong and the methods of pacing calculation in considerable detail.
translations.idiomatic: They then compiled a work in three scrolls entitled New Book of Yue Terrace Gnomon Shadows, reviewing earlier measurements' errors and setting out computational methods in detail.

sentences.zh: 既上奏，詔翰林學士范鎮為序以識。

translations.literal: After it was submitted, an edict directed Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen to write a preface as record.
translations.idiomatic: After it was presented to the throne, Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen was directed to write a preface for the record.

translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cong held that the shadow dimensions obtained for the twenty-four solar terms agreed more closely with Wang Pu's figures in the Xiande Qintian Calendar than earlier reckonings had.

sentences.zh: 後漢熹平三年，《四分曆》志立冬中景長一丈，立春中景長九尺六寸。

translations.literal: Later Han, third year of Xiaping: the Monograph on the Quarter-remainder Calendar records mid-term shadow at Start of Winter as 1 zhang and at Beginning of Spring as 9 chi 6 cun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xiaping era of Later Han, the Monograph on the Quarter-remainder Calendar records the mid-term shadow at Start of Winter as 1 zhang and at Beginning of Spring as 9 chi 6 cun.

sentences.zh: 尋冬至南極，日晷最長，二氣去至日數既同，則中景應等，而前長後短，頓差四寸。

translations.literal: Seeking the winter solstice at the southern pole, the sundial shadow is longest; since the two qi are equally distant from the solstice day in count, their mid-term shadows ought to be equal—yet the former is long and the latter short, suddenly differing by 4 cun.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice the sun stands at its southern limit and the gnomon shadow is longest. The two qi lie equally many days from the solstice, so their mid-term shadows should match; instead the earlier is longer and the later shorter—a sudden discrepancy of 4 cun.

sentences.zh: 此曆景冬至後天之驗也。

translations.literal: This is verification from the calendar's shadow data that the winter solstice lagged behind Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is proof from the calendar's shadow records that the winter solstice was placed late relative to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 二氣中景日差九分半弱，進退均調，略無盈縮，以率計之，二氣各退二日十二刻，則晷景之數，立冬更短，立春更長，並差二寸，二氣中景俱長九尺八寸矣，即立冬、立春之正日也。

translations.literal: The mid-term shadows of the two qi differ by nine fen and a half minus in daily rate; advancing and retreating evenly, there is scarcely excess or deficit. Calculating by the rate, if each of the two qi retreats two days and twelve ke, then the gnomon-shadow numbers would make Start of Winter's shadow shorter and Beginning of Spring's longer, each by 2 cun—and the mid-term shadows of both would be 9 chi 8 cun; that is the true day of Start of Winter and Beginning of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The two mid-term shadows differ by a daily rate of nine and a half fen minus; with even advance and retreat there is little surplus or shortfall. By that rate, if each qi is moved back two days and twelve ke, the shadow lengths would shorten at Start of Winter and lengthen at Beginning of Spring by 2 cun each—both mid-term shadows becoming 9 chi 8 cun, which would be the true days of Start of Winter and Beginning of Spring.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，曆置冬至後天亦二日十二刻也。

translations.literal: Extrapolating from this, the calendar's placement of the winter solstice also lagged behind Heaven by two days and twelve ke.
translations.idiomatic: By the same reasoning, the calendar's winter solstice also lagged Heaven by two days and twelve ke.

sentences.zh: 熹平三年，時曆丁丑冬至，加時正在日中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaping, the calendar of the time placed the winter solstice on dingchou, with the added hour exactly at noon.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaping year 3, the calendar then in use fixed the winter solstice on dingchou, with the added hour exactly at midday.

sentences.zh: 以二日十二刻減之，定以乙亥冬至，加時在夜半後二十八刻。

translations.literal: Subtracting two days and twelve ke, the winter solstice is fixed at yihai, with the added hour at twenty-eight ke after midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract two days and twelve ke, and the winter solstice falls on yihai, with the added hour twenty-eight ke after midnight.

sentences.zh: 《宋志》大明五年十月十日，景一丈七寸七分半；

translations.literal: Monograph of Song: fifth year of Daming, tenth month, tenth day—shadow 1 zhang 7 cun 7 fen and a half;
translations.idiomatic: The Monograph of Song records that in Daming year 5, tenth month, day 10, the shadow was 1 zhang 7 cun 7 fen and a half;

sentences.zh: 十一月二十五日，景一丈八寸一分太。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, twenty-fifth day—shadow 1 zhang 8 cun 1 fen excess.
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month, 1 zhang 8 cun 1 fen excess;

sentences.zh: 二十六日，一丈七寸五分強。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth day—1 zhang 7 cun 5 fen strong.
translations.idiomatic: and on the twenty-sixth, 1 zhang 7 cun 5 fen strong.

sentences.zh: 折取其中，則中天冬至應在十一月三日求其早晚。

translations.literal: Taking the mean between them, the midwinter solstice at the sky's center ought to fall on the third day of the eleventh month—thus determining whether it was early or late.
translations.idiomatic: Averaging these, the true midwinter solstice should fall on the third day of the eleventh month—whence one may determine how early or late it was.

sentences.zh: 令後二日景相減，則一日差率也，倍之為法。

translations.literal: Let the shadow of the two days after be subtracted from that of the two days before; the difference is the daily rate of change, which doubled becomes the divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the shadow of the two preceding days from that of the two following days; the difference is the daily rate, which doubled gives the divisor.

sentences.zh: 前二日減，以百刻乘之，為實。

translations.literal: Subtract the former two days' shadow, multiply by one hundred ke, and that is the dividend.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the shadow of the two earlier days, multiply by one hundred ke, and the product is the dividend.

sentences.zh: 以法除實，得冬至加時在夜半後三十一刻，在《元嘉曆》後一日，天數之正也。

translations.literal: Divide the dividend by the divisor; one obtains winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight, one day later than the Yuankai Calendar—the correct reckoning of heaven's days.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing the dividend by the divisor yields winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight—one day later than the Yuankai Calendar, which matches the true count of celestial days.

sentences.zh: 量檢彌年，則加減均同。

translations.literal: Measure and check over many years, and additions and subtractions are on average the same.
translations.idiomatic: Checked over many years, the additions and subtractions balance out evenly.

sentences.zh: 異歲相課，則遠近應率。

translations.literal: Compare different years, and distance and nearness correspond to the rate.
translations.idiomatic: Compared across different years, near and far dates align with the expected rate.

sentences.zh: 觀二家之說，略而未通。

translations.literal: Observing the two schools' doctrines, they are summary but not penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the two schools' theories shows them to be sketchy and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 熹平乃要取其中，而失於至前、至後之餘。

translations.literal: Xiping sought to take the mean but erred in the surplus before and after the solstices.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiping method aimed at a mean but missed the surplus before and after the solstices.

sentences.zh: 大明則左右率，而失於為實、為法之數。

translations.literal: Daming balanced the left-right rates but erred in the numbers for dividend and divisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Daming method balanced the left and right rates but erred in setting the dividend and divisor.

sentences.zh: 若夫較景、定氣，曆家最為急務。

translations.literal: As for comparing shadows and fixing qi, these are the calendrist's most urgent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing shadows and fixing the solar terms are the calendrist's most pressing duties.

sentences.zh: 觀古較驗，止以冬至前後數日之間，以定加時早晚。

translations.literal: Observing ancient comparisons, they stopped at only a few days before and after winter solstice to fix the added hour early or late.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier comparisons relied only on a few days before and after winter solstice to fix whether the added hour came early or late.

sentences.zh: 且景之差行，當二至前後，進退在微芒之間。

translations.literal: Moreover, the shadow's differing motion occurs around the two solstices, advancing and retreating within the finest gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the shadow's rate of change around the two solstices advances and retreats within the finest gradations.

sentences.zh: 又日有變行，盈縮稍異，若以為准，則加時相背。

translations.literal: Also the sun has variable motion, waxing and waning slightly differently; if taken as standard, the added hour will oppose each other.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's motion also varies, waxing and waning slightly; if that variation is taken as the standard, the added hour will be misaligned.

sentences.zh: 又晉、漢曆術，多以前後所測晷要取其中，此亦差過半日。

translations.literal: Also Jin and Han calendrical methods mostly took the mean of gnomon shadows measured before and after; this too errs by more than half a day.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Han calendar methods often averaged gnomon shadows measured before and after a term—an error of more than half a day.

sentences.zh: 今比歲較驗，在立冬、立春景移過寸，若較取加時，則宜以其相近者通計，半之為距至泛日；

translations.literal: Now comparing year by year, at Beginning of Winter and Beginning of Spring the shadow shifts more than an inch; if comparing to fix the added hour, one should take the nearest and compute together, halving to get the general day from solstice;
translations.idiomatic: Year-by-year comparison shows that at Beginning of Winter and Beginning of Spring the shadow shifts by more than an inch; to fix the added hour, the nearest observations should be combined and halved to obtain the general day from solstice;

sentences.zh: 乃以其晷數相減，餘者以法乘之，滿其日晷差而一，為刻；

translations.literal: then subtract their gnomon numbers; multiply the remainder by the divisor, and when it fills the day's gnomon difference, that is one mark;
translations.idiomatic: subtract the two gnomon readings; multiply the remainder by the divisor, and when it fills the day's gnomon difference, the quotient is one mark;

sentences.zh: 乃以差刻求冬至，視其前晷，多則為減，少則為加，求夏至返之。

translations.literal: then by the difference in marks seek winter solstice; looking at the preceding gnomon, if more then subtract, if less then add; seek summer solstice by reversing.
translations.idiomatic: use the mark-difference to find winter solstice: if the preceding gnomon reading is greater, subtract; if less, add; reverse the procedure for summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 加減距至泛日，為定日；

translations.literal: Add or subtract the general day from solstice to get the fixed day;
translations.idiomatic: Add or subtract the general day from solstice to obtain the fixed day;

sentences.zh: 仍加半日之刻，命從前距日辰，算外，即二至加時日辰及刻分。

translations.literal: still add half a day's marks, assign from the preceding distance day's double-hour, outside the calculation—that is the two solstices' added hour day double-hour and marks.
translations.idiomatic: add half a day's marks, assign from the preceding interval day's double-hour, and count outward to obtain the two solstices' added hour, double-hour, and marks.

sentences.zh: 如此推求，則二至加時早晚可驗矣。

translations.literal: Seeking thus, the two solstices' added hour early or late can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued in this way, whether the two solstices' added hour comes early or late can be verified.

sentences.zh: 皇祐岳台晷景法

translations.literal: Huangyou Yue Terrace Gnomon Shadow Method
translations.idiomatic: The Huangyou Yue Terrace Gnomon Shadow Method

sentences.zh: 按《大衍》載日及《崇天》定差之率，雖號通密，然未能盡上下交應之理，則晷度無由合契。

translations.literal: According to the Dayan's sun carriage and Chongtian's fixed-difference rate, though called thoroughly precise, they could not fully exhaust the principle of upper-lower mutual correspondence, so gnomon degrees had no way to match.
translations.idiomatic: The Dayan Calendar's sun carriage and the Chongtian Calendar's fixed-difference rate, though called thoroughly precise, could not fully capture the principle of mutual correspondence above and below, so gnomon degrees could not be made to agree.

sentences.zh: 今立新法，使上符盈縮之行，下參句股之數，所算尺寸與天測驗，無有先後。

translations.literal: Now a new method is established, making it accord above with waxing-waning motion and below consult gougu numbers; calculated dimensions and heavenly measurements have no priority or lag.
translations.idiomatic: A new method is now established to match the sun's waxing and waning above and the gougu ratios below, so calculated dimensions and celestial measurements agree without discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 其術曰：計二至後日數，乃減去二至約餘，仍加半日之分，即所求日午中積數，而置之以求進退差分，求進退差分者，置中積之數，如一象九十一日三十二分以下為在前；

translations.literal: The method says: compute days after the two solstices, subtract the two-solstice approximate remainder, still add half a day's parts—that is the sought day's noon accumulated number, and set it to seek advance-retreat difference; to seek advance-retreat difference, set the accumulated number: if one image's ninety-one days thirty-two fen or below, it is in the front;
translations.idiomatic: The method runs: count the days after the two solstices, subtract the solstice approximate remainder, and add half a day's fraction to obtain the sought day's noon accumulated number; set this to find the advance-retreat difference—if the accumulated number is ninety-one days thirty-two fen or less (one quadrant), it falls in the front section;

sentences.zh: 如一象以上，返減二至限一百八十二日六十一分，餘為在後。

translations.literal: If one image or above, inversely subtract the two-solstice limit of one hundred eighty-two days sixty-one fen; the remainder is in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: If it exceeds one quadrant, subtract it from the two-solstice limit of one hundred eighty-two days sixty-one fen; the remainder falls in the rear section.

sentences.zh: 置前後度於上，列二百於下，以上減下，餘以下乘上，滿四千一百三十五除之為分，不滿，退除為小分。

translations.literal: Set the front and rear degrees above, array two hundred below; subtract below from above, multiply the remainder by below and above, when it fills four thousand one hundred thirty-five divide to get fen; if not full, retreat-divide for small fen.
translations.idiomatic: Place the front and rear degrees above and two hundred below; subtract the lower from the upper, multiply the remainder by both values, divide by four thousand one hundred thirty-five to obtain fen, and any remainder becomes small fen.

sentences.zh: 在冬至後即為進差，在夏至後即為退差。

translations.literal: After winter solstice it is advance difference; after summer solstice it is retreat difference.
translations.idiomatic: After winter solstice the result is an advance difference; after summer solstice, a retreat difference.

sentences.zh: 仍列初、末二限，求入初、末限者，置所求日午中積數，日在冬至後初限、夏至後末限之數四十五日六十二分以下，即為所求在初限；

translations.literal: Still array the initial and final two limits; to seek entry into initial or final limit, set the sought day's noon accumulated number: if days after winter solstice initial limit or after summer solstice final limit are forty-five days sixty-two fen or below, that is sought in the initial limit;
translations.idiomatic: Next set the initial and final limits: if the sought day's noon accumulated number, counted from winter solstice in the initial limit or summer solstice in the final limit, is forty-five days sixty-two fen or less, it falls within the initial limit;

sentences.zh: 如在已上者，乃返減二至限，餘即為所求入末限。

translations.literal: If at or above that, inversely subtract the two-solstice limit; the remainder is sought entry into the final limit.
translations.idiomatic: If it exceeds that, subtract from the two-solstice limit; the remainder enters the final limit.

sentences.zh: 其冬至後末限、夏至後初限，以一百三十七日為率。

translations.literal: For winter solstice after final limit and summer solstice after initial limit, take one hundred thirty-seven days as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: For the period after winter solstice's final limit and after summer solstice's initial limit, use one hundred thirty-seven days as the rate.

sentences.zh: 用求午中晷數。

translations.literal: Use this to seek the noon gnomon number.
translations.idiomatic: This is used to find the noon gnomon reading.

sentences.zh: 求午中晷數者，視所求。

translations.literal: To seek the noon gnomon number, look at what is sought.
translations.idiomatic: To find the noon gnomon reading, consider which limit applies.

sentences.zh: 如入冬至後初限、夏至後末限者，以入限日減一千九百三十七半，餘為泛差；

translations.literal: If entering winter solstice after initial limit or summer solstice after final limit, subtract limit-entry days from one thousand nine hundred thirty-seven and a half; the remainder is the general difference;
translations.idiomatic: If within winter solstice's initial limit or summer solstice's final limit, subtract the limit-entry days from one thousand nine hundred thirty-seven and a half; the remainder is the general difference;

sentences.zh: 仍以限日分乘其進退差，五因百約之，用減泛差，為定差；

translations.literal: still multiply limit days and parts by the advance-retreat difference, reduce by five-times-one-hundred approximation, use to subtract from general difference—that is the fixed difference;
translations.idiomatic: multiply the limit days and fractional parts by the advance-retreat difference, reduce by the five-times-one-hundred factor, and subtract from the general difference to obtain the fixed difference;

sentences.zh: 乃以入限日分自相乘，以乘定差，滿一百萬為尺，不滿為寸、為分及小分，以減冬至常晷一丈二尺八寸五分，餘為其日午中晷數。

translations.literal: then square the limit-entry days and parts, multiply by the fixed difference; when it fills one million that is chi, if not full then cun, fen, and small fen; subtract from winter solstice's constant gnomon one zhang two chi eight cun five fen—the remainder is that day's noon gnomon number.
translations.idiomatic: square the limit-entry days and parts, multiply by the fixed difference, and convert at one million per chi (with remainder as cun, fen, and small fen); subtract from the winter solstice constant gnomon of one zhang two chi eight cun five fen to obtain that day's noon gnomon reading.

sentences.zh: 若所求入冬至後末限、夏至後初限者，乃三約入限日分，以減四百八十五少，餘為泛差；

translations.literal: If the sought enters winter solstice after final limit or summer solstice after initial limit, then third-approximate the limit-entry days and parts, subtract from four hundred eighty-five and a fraction less; the remainder is general difference;
translations.idiomatic: If the date falls in winter solstice's final limit or summer solstice's initial limit, reduce the limit-entry days and parts by one-third, subtract from four hundred eighty-five and a fraction, and the remainder is the general difference;

sentences.zh: 仍以進退差減極數，餘者若在春分後、秋分前者，直以四約之，以加泛差，為定差；

translations.literal: still subtract the advance-retreat difference from the extreme number; if the remainder is after spring equinox and before autumn equinox, directly quarter-approximate it and add to general difference—that is fixed difference;
translations.idiomatic: subtract the advance-retreat difference from the extreme number; if the date falls after spring equinox and before autumn equinox, quarter the remainder and add it to the general difference to obtain the fixed difference;

sentences.zh: 若在春分前、秋分後者，乃以去二分日數及分乘之，滿六百而一，以減泛差，餘為定差，用以入限日分自相乘，以乘定差，滿一百萬為尺，不滿為寸、為分及小分，以加夏至常晷一尺五寸七分，即為其日午中晷數。

translations.literal: If before spring equinox and after autumn equinox, then multiply days and parts from the equinox by it, when it fills six hundred that is one, subtract from general difference; the remainder is fixed difference; use it to square limit-entry days and parts, multiply fixed difference; when it fills one million that is chi, if not full then cun, fen, and small fen; add to summer solstice's constant gnomon one chi five cun seven fen—that is that day's noon gnomon number.
translations.idiomatic: If before spring equinox or after autumn equinox, multiply the days and parts from the equinox, divide by six hundred, subtract from the general difference to get the fixed difference; square the limit-entry days and parts, multiply by the fixed difference, convert at one million per chi, and add to the summer solstice constant gnomon of one chi five cun seven fen to obtain that day's noon gnomon reading.

sentences.zh: 若用周歲曆，直以其日晷景損益差分乘其日午中之余，滿法約之，乃損益其下晷數，即其日午中定晷。

translations.literal: If using the annual-cycle calendar, directly multiply that day's gnomon shadow wax-wane difference by that day's noon remainder, when it fills the divisor approximate it, then wax or wane the lower gnomon number—that is that day's noon fixed gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: With the annual-cycle calendar, multiply that day's gnomon wax-wane difference by the noon remainder, reduce by the divisor, and adjust the base gnomon reading to obtain the day's fixed noon gnomon.

sentences.zh: 如此推求，則上下通應之理，句股斜射之原，皆可視驗，乃具岳台晷景周歲算數。

translations.literal: Seeking thus, the principle of upper-lower mutual correspondence and the origin of gougu oblique projection can all be visually verified; then are furnished the Yue Terrace gnomon shadow annual-cycle calculation numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued in this way, the principle of mutual correspondence above and below and the basis of gougu oblique projection can all be checked against observation; the full annual-cycle calculation tables for Yue Terrace gnomon shadows follow.
